title: Sharp Bounds on Counterfactual Attribution Probabilities under a Kendall Tau Band
banked_reason: D0.5 repeatedly failed on load-bearing tau-band sharpness, endpoint regularity, and one-step CLT gaps; the last review still required new math beyond an in-place D0.R edit.
gap_reasons: Final D0.5 review stayed non-convergent after D0.R: band_envelope_smoothness_not_discharged@lem:tau-band-piecewise-smooth, band_envelope_branch_glue_unproved@lem:tau-band-piecewise-smooth, and the EIF/CLT results inherited that undischarged band smoothness.

The proof switched estimator objects in thm:regular-one-step-clt and used an unstated upstream expansion in lem:score-consistency, so the cross-fitted one-step CLT was not discharged from the declared primitive nuisance and sampling assumptions.

Earlier D0.5 rounds repeatedly flagged the sharpness bridge for the Kendall-tau band: citation_overreach_tau_band_interval@lem:tau-copula-attainment and missing interval-band/measurable-selector attainment for the exact sharp GPN interval.

The estimator/inference layer required new off-piece score and remainder control plus operational clipping/positivity structure; those were new mathematical or definition-level ingredients, not in-place D0.R edits.
proof_attempt_summary: The run tried to turn family-free Kendall-tau pointwise copula envelopes into a sharp continuous-GPN partial-ID theorem, then add regular-piece EIF and cross-fitted one-step endpoint inference. The proposal cleared Stage -0.5 at field tier, but D0.5 repeatedly found missing load-bearing mathematics: interval-band copula attainment/measurable selection, band-envelope smoothness, off-piece score and remainder control, and an estimator object mismatch in the one-step CLT. A retry should preserve the literature map and solver traces but first supply a real tau-band attainment theorem and a primitive estimator/inference construction, rather than reusing the current sharpness and CLT claims unchanged.
tldr: The proposal studies the population counterfactual attribution target theta = P(Y(0) < c_0 | Y(1) >= c_1) when the only cross-world information is that the conditional copula of (Y(1), Y(0)) has Kendall's tau in a prespecified band. Because this target depends on the joint law only through the point value C_x(m_1(x), m_0(x)), the identified set should be reducible to direct pointwise optimization over the copula class, using the best-possible Kendall-tau copula bounds rather than a parametric Gaussian path. In the band-regular same-piece regime, the scalar endpoints are ratio functionals with a well-defined efficient influence function; under tailored active-envelope nuisance product-rate conditions, that gradient supports the single declared cross-fitted one-step endpoint estimator. The remaining open inferential content is uniform coverage for the full tau-indexed endpoint curve when the active closed-form copula piece switches.
gap: Continuous-outcome attribution now has observed-event GPN bounds and parametric-copula sensitivity analyses, but no family-free sharp theorem for the analogous population counterfactual target under an interpretable concordance restriction and no endpoint inference theory for that object.
fill: The project fills that gap by converting the causal problem into Kendall-constrained pointwise copula optimization, then attaching a population EIF characterization, a regular-regime orthogonal endpoint estimator, and a tau-uniform inference conjecture tailored to active-piece switches.
